q.schemeNote: The Irish scheme prints “Clóraplast” for the green pigment. The English scheme for this same question gives “Chlorophyll”. The original Irish scheme is shown unchanged.

The Irish scheme explicitly describes a method name plus two matching points (3 × 3 marks). The English scheme allows the name to count as one of three points. Follow the instructions in the displayed edition.

The Irish scheme prints 4 + 4 + 6 + 6 for Q9(f), while the English scheme prints 4 + 4 + 4 + 6. The Irish allocations therefore total 62 for the printed 60-mark question. This source discrepancy is preserved.

For Q12(a)(iii), the Irish scheme says four points; the English scheme says three but prints four awards. For Q12(d)(ii), the Irish scheme prints 4 + 4 + 6 + 6 (20); the English scheme prints 4 + 4 + 4 + 6 (18). The Irish Q12(d) allocations total its printed 30 marks.

Source lettering differs: the Irish pig crosses use C/c, but the Irish scheme retains E/e. Read E, e, EE and Ee in that scheme as C, c, CC and Cc respectively. The pea passage also uses A/a where the English paper uses T/t.
